name: Senegal
summary_text: Senegal is dangerous for trans visitors. The Penal Code criminalises “unnatural acts” (up to 5 years, applied to both men and women), enforcement is active (periodic arrest waves), and anti-LGBT forces are pushing to raise sentences to 15 years. Mob violence against perceived LGBT people is documented, and even public discussion is policed: two men were jailed in 2024 for “false news” after accusing the Prime Minister of tolerating homosexuality. There is no legal gender recognition and no visible community infrastructure — Dakar's scene is deeply underground. For a visitor: visible trans presentation risks arrest and mob violence.

sources.claim_summary: Human Dignity Trust country profile: Senegal criminalises same-sex sexual activity (Article 319 of the 1965 Penal Code, up to 5 years' imprisonment). (Only the opening of the profile was retrievable at fetch time.)

sources.title: Senegal: 15 years in prison for being LGBT ?
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (July 2024): anti-LGBT forces in Senegal seek longer prison time - after PM Sonko alleged homosexuality is 'tolerated', MP Cheikh Abdou Bara Dolly Mbacké proposed a bill mirroring a failed 2022 initiative raising sentences to 10-15 years for 'offences of bisexuality [including homosexuality], transsexuality, necrophilia and zoophilia' plus fines up to 5 million CFA francs; abuses against LGBT+ people are commonplace.

sources.title: Senegal gay rights: Two jailed for criticising Ousmane Sonko
sources.claim_summary: BBC (June 2024): two men jailed in Senegal for 'spreading false news' after accusing PM Sonko of tolerating homosexuality - activist Bah Diakhate and Imam Ndao received three months and fines; Sonko had said homosexuality was 'not accepted, but tolerated' after a French politician expressed support for same-sex marriage at a Dakar student forum.

US State Department 2012 Human Rights Report for Senegal: documents preelectoral violence, torture, and 'violence and discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) persons' among major human-rights problems.

sources.title: 4 anti-gay arrests in Senegal as 2019 election approaches
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (Sept 2018): a wave of politically motivated anti-gay arrests as the 2019 election approached - two women and two men detained in Dakar for 'acts against the order of nature'; Arc en Ciel Senegal: 'The hunt for sexual minorities begins' as the government defends itself against 'pro-homosexual' accusations; Pan Africa ILGA called for accountability.

sources.title: Man's body dug up and burned in the street 'after it was revealed he was gay' | News World | Metro News
sources.claim_summary: Metro (Nov 2023): a man's body was exhumed and set on fire in the street after locals found out he was gay - a case that shocked Senegal, where homosexuality is punishable with prison time.
